declared.title: Testing the boundaries of the choice overload phenomenon: The effect of number of options and time pressure on decision difficulty and satisfaction
declared.foundIn: recherche Crossref « choice overload culture cross-cultural moderator number of options satisfaction » du 2026-11-22 (dossier too-many-choices) ; titre relevé sur Crossref : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: participants choosing one prize for a draw among 3 or 10 descriptions, with limited or extended time; country not given in the abstract

findings.text: Choosing among 10 prizes rather than 3 left people less satisfied with their decision, but not more regretful

support.sentence: The larger set of alternatives led to less satisfaction, but not less regret, with people's decisions.

findings.text: With little time, choosing among many prizes felt harder and more frustrating than in the other conditions

support.sentence: Participants given a limited amount of time to choose with a larger set of alternatives found their decisions to be more difficult and frustrating than did participants in the other conditions.

limits: a prize draw: a choice of little importance
sample size not given in the abstract
one study, one author, 3 vs 10 options only
